comment: The objective of eliminating unnecessary duplicate data entry is strongly supported, but “captured once” should not be formulated as an unconditional rule applying to all health information. Clinical information may legitimately be generated, verified or recorded by different actors at different points in a care pathway, and provenance must be preserved. The principle is most directly applicable to authoritative reference data and to avoiding duplicate administrative/reporting collection. Similarly, data collected for one purpose cannot automatically be made available “wherever it is needed”; reuse remains subject to lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation and other applicable safeguards. Finally, “consent and permissions” should not imply that consent is always the relevant legal basis. Under the GDPR, health data may also be processed for healthcare delivery and management, substantial public interest, public health, research and statistical purposes under defined conditions.
